method: Direct header, implementation and class-test audit; no C++ build or execution. The six formatting literals are transcribed from the class test and independently re-derived from the source's std::setprecision(4) general format.
evidence_tier: tier 3 (source review, transcribed class-test literals) and tier 4 (independently derived formatting boundaries, native /proc readings and report assembly)

source_anchors.operation: bytesToHumanReadable divides by 1024 through a six-entry unit table and prints with std::setprecision(4) in the general format, so trailing zeros are dropped and no value below 1024 reaches scientific notation
exhausting the unit table returns the literal string "Congrats. That's a lot of bytes: " followed by the count; reachable from 2^60 bytes upwards
the Linux working-set reading is statm.resident * sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE) / 1024, the same counter /proc/self/status publishes as VmRSS already in kibibytes
free memory prefers MemAvailable from /proc/meminfo and falls back to sysconf(_SC_AVPHYS_PAGES) * sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE) / 1024, which glibc answers from MemAvailable then MemFree
the Linux peak reading is getrusage(...).ru_maxrss, already in kibibytes, which is the counter /proc/self/status publishes as VmHWM
delta() and usage() call after() when mem_after == 0, so a genuine zero reading is indistinguishable from an unrecorded one and is resampled on every print
the peak part of a report is emitted only when mem_after_peak > 0, which is the source's own test for platform support
diff_str_ appends "-" to a local string and then assigns over that string instead of appending, so the minus sign is discarded and every reported delta reads as an increase

class_test_review.literal_extraction: All six bytesToHumanReadable literals are transcribed. The memory section's shape is reproduced without its 20 MB mzML fixture: a 64 MiB allocation is made resident page by page and the same 'grew by more than 10 000 KB' assertion is made, which removes a format dependency from a SYSTEM test.

cpp_issues.summary: SysInfo::MemUsage::diff_str_ builds the minus sign into a local string and then overwrites that string with the magnitude, so a shrinking working set is reported as an increase.
cpp_issues.trigger: MemUsage u; /* free memory */ u.delta("release") with mem_after < mem_before prints "3 MB" where it means "-3 MB".
cpp_issues.proposed_fix: Change the assignment on the following line to an append, or build the sign into the same expression.
cpp_issues.rust_handling: Not reproduced. system::sys_info emits the sign, and the divergence is documented at the item and in docs/SYS_INFO_SUPPORT.md.

native_boundaries: Every memory reading is Option<u64>: Linux answers from /proc, and every other platform answers None rather than a fabricated zero
The source's Windows PROCESS_MEMORY_COUNTERS_EX and macOS Mach task_info / host_statistics64 branches have no counterpart, because both need a platform binding this crate does not take

The working set is read from /proc/self/status VmRSS and the peak from VmHWM, which the kernel derives from the same counters the source reaches through statm and getrusage, already in kibibytes and without a sysconf call
Free memory reads MemAvailable then MemFree, reproducing glibc's own answer to _SC_AVPHYS_PAGES without the libc call
/proc reads are capped at 256 KiB and require the kB unit on the matched line, which the source does not check
MemUsage models 'not recorded' as None rather than the source's 0 sentinel, so a genuine zero reading is not resampled
MemUsage::delta refuses an event label above 1 MiB; the source applies no bound
A negative working-set delta keeps its sign, which the source discards
process_id returns u32 from std::process::id rather than the source's Int64, because no platform identifier needs the sign or the width
openmp_gap: SysInfo carries no #pragma omp; there is no parallel behaviour to reproduce.
